HTTP RPC client for sending JSON-RPC requests and parsing responses.

# Purpose
`fd_rpc_client.c` implements a non-blocking HTTP client for RPC requests. It manages a fixed set of request slots in `fd_rpc_client_t`, opens TCP sockets to the configured RPC address and port, sends JSON-RPC `POST` requests, and polls for send and receive progress. The file also provides [`fd_rpc_client_new`](<#fd_rpc_client_new>) to initialize the client, [`fd_rpc_client_wait_ready`](<#fd_rpc_client_wait_ready>) to test server reachability, [`fd_rpc_client_service`](<#fd_rpc_client_service>) to advance all active requests, [`fd_rpc_client_status`](<#fd_rpc_client_status>) to query request state, and [`fd_rpc_client_close`](<#fd_rpc_client_close>) to release a request slot.

The file defines two request helpers, [`fd_rpc_client_request_latest_block_hash`](<#fd_rpc_client_request_latest_block_hash>) and [`fd_rpc_client_request_transaction_count`](<#fd_rpc_client_request_transaction_count>), which build JSON-RPC bodies for `getLatestBlockhash` and `getTransactionCount`. It parses HTTP responses with `picohttpparser`, reads the `Content-Length` header, and decodes the JSON body with `cJSON`. For `getTransactionCount`, it extracts the numeric `result` field. For `getLatestBlockhash`, it extracts the nested `result.value.blockhash` string and decodes it from Base58 into 32 bytes with `fd_base58_decode_32`. The code returns explicit error codes for network errors, malformed responses, oversized messages, and too many active requests.
